what: The photo strip is pinned to the screen and flows horizontally by as much as the vertical scroll (2D canvas). Photos are .92 of the strip height, with width min(.66 × width, .76 × height), gap min(30, width/48) and end margins of 4.22% of width (16 below 600px). When scrolling is fast (max at horizontal speed 1800px/s), the squash strength jumps up to .65, and each photo is cut into 3px vertical slices and drawn with the center slices squashed in height down to .75x (.93x at the edges). The squash follows that strength at 12/s and the strength cools at 6/s, so it flattens out within 1 second after stopping (30fps). Dragging the strip or rolling the horizontal wheel also scrolls the page by the same amount

options.squeeze: Minimum height ratio of the center piece (at max press), default .75
options.edge: Share that is pressed less toward the edges, default .18 (.93× at the edge)
options.kick: Max press strength kicked by one fast scroll, default .65
options.speed: Horizontal speed (px/s) at which the squash is at its maximum, default 1800
options.top: Top offset for pinning (px, header height above), default 0 — put the same value in --fx-top too
options.[data-fx-part=viewport]: Band board — contains canvas and list
options.[data-fx-part=photo]: Photo (data-focus sets vertical alignment 0~1) or a placeholder panel (.wf-img data-label) — the panel draws background color, diagonals and label

use: …
note: The original scrolls inside an inner scroll panel (.join-page) — if it is an inner panel, put data-fx-scroller on that panel. On phones, dragging is not intercepted and only flows as vertical scroll

from.where: join.html .join-gallery (strip of studio photos below the application page)
